docs.text: Tortles ¶ Tortles are a long-lived, patient, and coastal people most strongly associated with the Myruun Clans of northern Arkhaven . Myruun Clan Houses ¶ The Myruun Clans are dominated by tortles. Their coastal settlements, river shrines, shell-marked houses, fishing grounds, and elder councils form the core of Myruun society. Tortles are well suited to the region’s jungle rivers, mangrove belts, sea cliffs, flooded lowlands, and scar-adjacent waters. Their long lives, defensive habits, coastal skill, river knowledge, and respect for old boundaries make them natural leaders among the Myruun. Patience and Memory ¶ Tortle culture values patience, oathkeeping, shrine duty, navigation, fishing rights, controlled hospitality, and long memory. Tortle elders hold high status because they remember floods, treaties, monster migrations, lost routes, and disputes that younger peoples would forget. Outside Myruun lands, tortles are often seen as calm travellers, river guides, shrine keepers, fishermen, and slow-speaking negotiators. In truth, their patience should not be mistaken for weakness. Tortle communities are difficult to move, difficult to frighten, and very difficult to make forget an insult.

docs.text: The Myruun Clans are dominated by tortles. Their coastal settlements, river shrines, shell-marked houses, fishing grounds, and elder councils form the core of Myruun society. Tortles are well suited to the region’s jungle rivers, mangrove belts, sea cliffs, flooded lowlands, and scar-adjacent waters. Their long lives, defensive habits, coastal skill, river knowledge, and respect for old boundaries make them natural leaders among the Myruun.
docs.title: Myruun Clan Houses

docs.text: Tortle culture values patience, oathkeeping, shrine duty, navigation, fishing rights, controlled hospitality, and long memory. Tortle elders hold high status because they remember floods, treaties, monster migrations, lost routes, and disputes that younger peoples would forget. Outside Myruun lands, tortles are often seen as calm travellers, river guides, shrine keepers, fishermen, and slow-speaking negotiators. In truth, their patience should not be mistaken for weakness. Tortle communities are difficult to move, difficult to frighten, and very difficult to make forget an insult.
docs.title: Patience and Memory

docs.text: Session 1: The Man in the River ¶ Played: 22 June 2026 Location: Morfael Starting point: Chapel of the Last Lantern The Chapel of the Last Lantern ¶ The party first gathered at the Chapel of the Last Lantern in Morfael, where Sister Halva Dorn formally introduced them to one another. The meeting was not dressed up as ceremony or prophecy. It was practical, urgent, and rooted in the sort of work Morfael knows too well: missing people, river rumours, suspicious cargo, and the dead washing up where the living would rather not look. Each member of the group had been drawn to the chapel for their own reason. Some already knew of one another from previous encounters or from reputation, but this was the first time they stood together with a common purpose. Sister Dorn laid out the immediate trouble. Cargo manifests had surfaced in connection with questionable freight, and Alekthar quickly concluded that they were false. Cassian already had knowledge of the missing folk in town, having counselled families who had been left without answers. Dorn also gave Cassian a list of missing names, placing the scattered grief of Morfael into something more concrete than rumour. Teclis had been sent by Arch-Lector Voss to investigate rumours of undeath in the area. Nakoa had received quiet word through Rennic Sallow that a courier had gone missing, and that the matter was worth his attention. Sister Dorn also told them of a young lad who had seen a body rise from the water after being washed against the Flood Steps near the Black Eel Market. There were also rumours of another body passing further downriver from higher in the city. The current was expected to bring it to Morfael before mid-morning. With that, the party left the chapel and made their way toward the market. The Black Eel Market ¶ The Black Eel Market was already awake by the time the party arrived: wet boards, eel tubs, cheap smoke, shouting traders, gulls over the river, and the smell of fish, mud, lamp oil, and cooked meat thick in the air. Cassian and Nakoa joined Lysa and Lerris at a table. There they learned that Lysa had previously seen a military-style bandage marked with a small stamp, though she had allowed it to wash further downriver before realising its significance. The market folk also spoke of cloaked figures seen in the area, seemingly scouting the streets and waterside routes even in broad daylight. Lerris offered food, and Nakoa made a strong early impression by enjoying more than one chicken drumstick. Meanwhile, Alekthar and Teclis spoke with Tovin, the young witness who had seen the earlier figure rise from the river. Tovin described a man whose skin shone with gold before he walked away muttering strange sentences. In return for his information, Teclis gave Tovin a gold coin, though the coin was only an illusion conjured by his magic. As the party gathered their separate threads of information and began to discuss what they had learned, Tovin suddenly spotted another shape in the water. Edrin Vaal at the Flood Steps ¶ The body drifted out of the River Oryn and struck the Flood Steps below the market. It was waterlogged, grey, and heavy with river filth. When the party turned it over, they recognised the dead man as Edrin Vaal, the missing courier. Edrin had medical bandages around his wrists that matched Lysa’s description. On his wrist was a brand: S-V-AUG-03 . Cassian and Nakoa, while trying to understand whether anything could be done for him, noticed red dust collected around his teeth and under his nails. There were also puncture marks around his neck. Then something changed. Nakoa felt a tingle crawl down his spine. His markings began to glow. Beneath Edrin’s grey skin, dark vein-like lines flickered with gold flecks and a pulsing red light. His back arched hard enough to scrape against the stone. His eyes opened, red and bloodshot, and unnatural strength surged through his body. The man who should have been dead rose from the steps. The Fight at the River ¶ Edrin attacked in a panic, more like a man reliving pain than a man making choices. A pulse of force erupted from him, pushing the party back as though gravity had faltered for a heartbeat. Alekthar reacted quickly, blessing the party while clutching the heirloom at his neck. Edrin struck at Nakoa with a glowing red fist, but could not break through the shimmering protection around the tabaxi. He then leapt at Cassian, before fixing his gaze on Teclis and tearing him through the air until the wizard was dragged within punching distance. At first, the party’s response carried compassion and self-defence. Edrin was a victim as much as a threat. But as the violence escalated, hesitation faded. Lightning crackled from a shocking grasp. Rapiers cut into deadened flesh. Divine power blazed through steel. Then a great wave of energy spilled from Edrin and struck the party, the market regulars, and everyone close enough to feel it. For an instant, Morfael vanished. They saw a darkened world beneath thunderous clouds. Red lightning split the sky. A grim pressure settled over everything, and a voice splintered through their minds one by one. The world breathes. As do I... Beneath your rivers. Within your walls. I have laid in waiting. Your towers rose. Your prayers echoed. Your kings called themselves eternal. You feel me now. In the water. In the stone. In your blood. My reach is unending. The world was never yours. It was merely sleeping above me. This is not my coming. This is my return. The townsfolk broke and ran screaming, but the newly formed party held their ground. Alekthar lost all composure. He screamed as though in agony and released a bolt of golden energy at the reawakened courier. Teclis, thinking quickly, conjured an illusion of dark energy within the water behind Edrin. The illusion called to him, and Edrin, unable to see the deception, moved toward it as if longing to join it. Instead, he crushed the stone steps beneath him in pain and anguish, leaving Nakoa and Cassian just out of reach. Nakoa and Cassian pressed the attack with their blades, one raw and swift, the other sharpened by divine force. The onslaught continued until Cassian delivered the final blow. With a decisive smite, he carved through Edrin’s body and brought the horror at the Flood Steps to an end. After the Surge ¶ When the fight ended, Edrin Vaal lay destroyed at the river’s edge. The market had scattered in terror, leaving the party amid broken stone, river water, and the silence that follows panic. The body was inspected after being pulled fully from the water. Cassian gave Edrin last rites, granting what dignity he could to a man who had clearly suffered before death and after it. While Cassian prayed, Alekthar considered some of the words Edrin had muttered during the fight and inspected the remains for further clues. Teclis and Nakoa made sketches and notes of the scene, recording the body, the river steps, the brand, the red dust, and what had just occurred. Their work was interrupted by Watch-Corporal Dannel Strake. Strake arrived with the authority of a man who wanted order restored quickly and with as little upper-city interference as possible. The exchange began poorly. A few unpleasant remarks were made, assumptions followed, and apologies came from both sides once the first heat had passed. Strake told the party that he would have to report what had happened upward to the city. He would give them ten minutes to gather themselves and move on before the matter became harder to manage. The party worried that Strake was trying to prevent Caer Oryn from looking too closely into Morfael for the wrong reasons, but he reassured them as best he could. He did not want disruption in the town, either for himself or for the people who lived there. If handing over the body and saying less kept Caer Oryn officials from pointing fingers at the local community, he would rather do that. Strake also advised that this was not the first such incident. Edrin was the third body said to have reanimated: one had been reported a week earlier, and another a month before that. Recognising Edrin, Strake gave the party directions to Gullhook Loft, the small cramped room where Vaal had been known to stay. He wished them well enough, and told them that if they needed him, Sister Dorn would know where to find him. The Walk to Gullhook Loft ¶ The path from the Flood Steps to Gullhook Loft was not long, but Morfael made it feel narrower than it was. The party left the open river behind and moved through damp lanes pressed between patched roofs, stained walls, leaning timber, and the sour smell of wet rope and old smoke. Behind them, the market was still recovering. Ahead of them was Edrin Vaal’s room, and whatever he had thought worth hiding before the river took him. As they walked, Nakoa returned to the moment that had unsettled him most. Edrin had struck him, yet the blow had failed to land. Something had stood between fist and flesh. The others recognised the shape of it as magic, but that answer did not sit easily with him. Nakoa did not think of himself as magical. Not in the way Cassian called upon divine strength, nor in the way Teclis shaped the world through study, discipline, and long elven training. The question turned into a small exchange between them: where power came from, what it looked like, and whether it had to announce itself before it could be real. Teclis, by way of demonstration, conjured the image of a succulent roast chicken, rich enough in scent and appearance to tempt even after the morning’s horror. Nakoa tried to take what was offered and found only absence beneath the promise of meat. The joke carried them a little further through the gloom. Then, with more confidence than certainty, Nakoa tried to imitate the trick. The result was rougher than Teclis’ work, less polished and less convincing, but undeniably present: a cooked chicken formed from illusion, called up by a tabaxi who had only moments before insisted he was not magical at all. Gullhook Loft ¶ Gullhook Loft sat above the street like an afterthought, its access reached by an exterior stair fixed to the side of the building. At the gable end, beneath the damp pitch of the roof, a small locked door marked the room where Edrin Vaal had been staying. Nakoa set to work with his picks, but the lock resisted him. After a few tense attempts, Alekthar placed a steadying hand on his shoulder and lent him guidance. With that quiet help, the mechanism gave way, and the party slipped inside. The room was cramped, damp, and deliberately plain. There was little comfort in it: a hammock bed, a pillow, a small writing board, courier tags, wax scraps, and the stale feeling of a place used for sleeping between jobs rather than living. Teclis cast light upon the pillow, and the sudden brightness exposed the room’s meagre contents in hard detail. Nakoa recognised the courier tags. He had seen their like before and understood enough of their markings to identify the most recent route. Whatever Edrin had been carrying, or arranging to carry, it pointed toward Magpie Lane in the Foundry Quarter of Caer Oryn. The party pressed the search further. The room looked bare by design, but not untouched. In the cast light, Alekthar caught the faint disturbance of dust along one floorboard. At almost the same moment, Nakoa noticed a chip in the wood that did not match ordinary wear. Different eyes, different instincts, the same answer: something had been hidden below. They lifted the secret panel and found a small bundle concealed beneath the floor. Inside was a piece of cloth. Nakoa recognised its material and weaving as something that could only have come from the Veylrain Expanse. Wrapped within it was a red candle whose wax carried a faint gold shimmer, and a small wooden idol shaped like a stamp. The base had been carved to match the sigil of House Amakiir. End of Session ¶ The session closed on that discovery: Edrin Vaal dead, the market shaken, Watch-Corporal Strake buying the party only a narrow window, and a hidden bundle beneath Gullhook Loft tying together Veylrain cloth, red-gold wax, courier work, Caer Oryn, and the stolen shape of House Amakiir authority. What began as a body in the river had become something wider. Morfael had shown the party its first corpse, its first clue, and its first warning that the trouble beneath the city was already moving in daylight.
docs.title: Session 1: The Man in the River

docs.text: Session 2: Foundries & Figurines ¶ Played: 29 June 2026 Location: Morfael to Caer Oryn Starting point: Gullhook Loft Leaving Gullhook Loft ¶ After leaving Gullhook Loft, the party made their way back into the streets of Morfael and began heading toward Caer Oryn. The discoveries beneath Edrin Vaal’s floorboards remained unresolved: Veylrain cloth, a red-gold candle, courier tags pointing toward Magpie Lane, and a small wooden stamp carved with the sigil of House Amakiir. Morfael was growing busier as the morning moved on. Streets filled with workers, traders, carts, and townsfolk already passing rumours between one another after the disturbance at the Flood Steps. Caer Oryn’s Morning Post ¶ As the party passed near Vellum House, a small working boy dropped a stack of fresh copies of Caer Oryn’s Morning Post on the steps. The headline caught the attention of several members of the party. HOUSE VAELISAR SEALED BY CIVIC DIRECTORATE ¶ The Civic Directorate confirmed this morning that House Vaelisar, noble house of the High Quarter, has been placed under formal seal. Directorate officers entered the Vaelisar townhouse shortly before dawn. Household staff were removed for questioning. The family residence, private chapel room, records office, and carriage house have all been closed under civic authority. A short notice posted outside the property states that the action concerns inheritance irregularity, unauthorised religious practice, and failure to comply with household registration law. No deaths have been confirmed by the Directorate at this time. The Vaelisar arms were covered by black cloth at third bell. This is normally done when a noble house is under investigation, dissolved, or placed into temporary civic custody. House Vaelisar is one of the remaining old aasimar bloodlines still recognised in Caer Oryn. Its sudden sealing has drawn comparison to the earlier fall of House Amakiir, though officials have not linked the two cases. The Directorate has advised citizens to avoid the sealed property and to report any Vaelisar retainers, documents, or goods found outside lawful custody. No further statement has been issued. The news raised eyebrows among the group, especially from Alekthar. The mention of House Amakiir gave the notice an immediate personal weight. The Road Out of Morfael ¶ The party continued through Morfael and followed the river out toward the open fields. The town thinned behind them as they left the tighter streets and moved onto the road toward Caer Oryn. The journey to the outskirts took roughly forty-five minutes. Ahead, the walls of Caer Oryn came fully into view. The First Gate ¶ As the party approached the first gate, they saw the walls of Caer Oryn up close. The sun began to appear from behind the city’s silhouette and above the horizon. All of the party except Cassian noticed something unusual: a visible black spot on the accretion disc of the Crown Magnetar. It had not been there the day before. When the others pointed it out to Cassian, he looked up in awe. He had spent years searching the sky for clues about the world’s existence, its place in the universe, and the order of the heavens above Lazuril. This was new. It was something he had not seen before. Into Caer Oryn ¶ After passing through the first gate, the party entered Caer Oryn. The capital was already stirring with the pressures of the day: city traffic, working crowds, and the early signs of preparation for Cadris’ Day. Once inside, Nakoa arranged for a letter to be sent back home. The full contents of the letter have not yet been disclosed, but a response is expected in roughly four days. Entry to the Foundry Quarter ¶ The party then made their way toward the Foundry Quarter. Entry was more difficult than usual because of the preparations for Cadris’ Day. Banners were being hung, work crews were moving through the streets, and the quarter had the ordered disorder of a city preparing itself for public celebration while still trying to keep its industry moving. Two guards blocked the main entry point into the quarter. Teclis attempted to overrule them using his position as Inquisitor-Scriptor, but without proper papers and authority from Voss, the guards refused to let the party through. To create a distraction, Teclis conjured the image and sound of the wife of the guard he was speaking to being intimate with the guard’s best mate and shift-partner, who was standing beside him. The illusion had the intended effect. Horrified by what he appeared to witness, the guard turned on his companion, and the pair began arguing long enough for the group to slip past. The party were not entirely unnoticed, but the guards had more immediate personal concerns to deal with. 17 Magpie Lane ¶ The party headed to Magpie Lane and found number 17. Rather than an active office or working address, the building was derelict. A local worker confirmed that it had once served as an office for a shift manager, but no one had worked there in months. Inside, dust had built up in the front room. The place had the stale stillness of a building left unused rather than simply left quiet. In the back room, however, there were signs of a struggle. A chair had been broken, and a table had been overturned. The group searched more closely and noticed a sealed passageway in the back room. Along the vertical line of the hidden door, there was a small hole covered by an illusion of brick mortar. Beyond it was a route down into a hidden basement. The Hidden Basement ¶ The basement beneath 17 Magpie Lane was filled with barrels. Most appeared to contain old vegetables and simple stores, but tucked behind the barrels was a small gilded chest. At the top of the chest, a small piece of string was exposed. The group approached it cautiously and decided that Nakoa should pull it free. The string was attached to a courier tag similar to the one found in Edrin’s room. Courier: Edrin Vaal Address: 17 Magpie Lane Item: small green lizard figure, Veylrain origin The party did not find or recover the figurine itself. The courier tag only confirmed that such an item had been linked to Edrin Vaal and 17 Magpie Lane. On the advice of the group, Nakoa checked the chest more carefully for traps. He found a small spring-loaded mechanism inside and disabled it before unlocking the chest. The trap had been arranged to smash together a vial of poison and a vial of alchemist’s fire. Beneath the mechanism was more Veylrain cloth. As the group continued their search, they also found blood seeping between the basement floorboards. There were dragged footmarks leading back toward the stairs, suggesting that someone had been wounded or moved through the basement after the struggle above. The blood was human. After securing the dangerous vials and inspecting the surrounding barrels, the party found only old vegetables and simple stored goods. With the chest dealt with and the courier tag recovered, they left 17 Magpie Lane. The Blacksmith of Magpie Lane ¶ Upon leaving number 17, Teclis and Cassian spoke with a local blacksmith working a few doors down. The blacksmith confirmed that he had seen people entering the derelict building a few days earlier. One of them matched the description of Halwin, and cloaked figures followed shortly after. He also heard signs of a scuffle from the building, but he had decided that it was not his business to investigate. He told the party that there was no ordinary way out of Magpie Lane without passing his forge. If the people involved had not come back past him, then they must have left by the closed-off section at the end of the lane. That end of the street formed a small cul-de-sac, with only a large sewer drain and scaffolding leading upward toward the rooftops. The End of the Lane ¶ The party travelled down Magpie Lane and inspected the closed-off area. The sewer drain was large enough for someone to climb down through, while the scaffolding was easy enough to climb for anyone skilled or desperate enough. As they were checking the area, Cassian was struck in the chest by a crossbow bolt. A figure on the rooftop quickly moved behind a chimney tower. Nakoa gave chase at once, climbing after the attacker while the others kept their distance below. Cassian healed himself and, in the moment after the wound closed, realised how far beyond him the magic of Teclis and Alekthar seemed to be. He had learned to smite his enemies, but he had not yet learned to channel divine power into more controlled and practised magic. Rooftop Chase ¶ Nakoa fired his bow at the rooftop figure and pointed the attacker out to the rest of the party, giving those below a clear line of sight. Two daggers flew back at Nakoa and wounded him badly, but he pressed on. Teclis created the illusion of a ladder beneath the cloaked figure, causing the attacker to waste precious moments kicking and reacting to something that was not truly there. That brief delay was enough for Nakoa to close the gap. The chase continued across the rooftops. Both Nakoa and the cloaked figure leapt a gap between buildings, bringing the pursuit into range of the rest of the party below. Alekthar judged the movement of the target and called down sacred flame from the sky. Teclis followed with the tolling force of Toll the Dead, a familiar staple of his magic. Between those strikes, Nakoa’s pressure, and a swipe from his rapier, the cloaked figure finally lost their footing. The figure stumbled and fell from the roof, crashing into a barrel below. They landed unconscious and prone, leaving the party to decide what to do next. End Point So Far ¶ The session notes currently end with the cloaked rooftop attacker unconscious after falling from the roof at the end of Magpie Lane.

The discoveries beneath Edrin Vaal’s floorboards remained unresolved: Veylrain cloth, a red-gold candle, courier tags pointing toward Magpie Lane, and a small wooden stamp carved with the sigil of House Amakiir. Morfael was growing busier as the morning moved on. Streets filled with workers, traders, carts, and townsfolk already passing rumours between one another after the disturbance at the Flood Steps.

docs.text: As the party passed near Vellum House, a small working boy dropped a stack of fresh copies of Caer Oryn’s Morning Post on the steps. The headline caught the attention of several members of the party.
docs.title: Caer Oryn’s Morning Post

docs.text: The Civic Directorate confirmed this morning that House Vaelisar, noble house of the High Quarter, has been placed under formal seal. Directorate officers entered the Vaelisar townhouse shortly before dawn. Household staff were removed for questioning. The family residence, private chapel room, records office, and carriage house have all been closed under civic authority. A short notice posted outside the property states that the action concerns inheritance irregularity, unauthorised religious practice, and failure to comply with household registration law. No deaths have been confirmed by the Directorate at this time. The Vaelisar arms were covered by black cloth at third bell. This is normally done when a noble house is under investigation, dissolved, or placed into temporary civic custody. House Vaelisar is one of the remaining old aasimar bloodlines still recognised in Caer Oryn. Its sudden sealing has drawn comparison to the earlier fall of House Amakiir, though officials have not linked the two cases. The Directorate has advised citizens to avoid the sealed property and to report any Vaelisar retainers, documents, or goods found outside lawful custody. No further statement has been issued. The news raised eyebrows among the group, especially from Alekthar. The mention of House Amakiir gave the notice an immediate personal weight.

docs.text: The party continued through Morfael and followed the river out toward the open fields. The town thinned behind them as they left the tighter streets and moved onto the road toward Caer Oryn. The journey to the outskirts took roughly forty-five minutes. Ahead, the walls of Caer Oryn came fully into view.
docs.title: The Road Out of Morfael

docs.text: As the party approached the first gate, they saw the walls of Caer Oryn up close. The sun began to appear from behind the city’s silhouette and above the horizon. All of the party except Cassian noticed something unusual: a visible black spot on the accretion disc of the Crown Magnetar. It had not been there the day before. When the others pointed it out to Cassian, he looked up in awe. He had spent years searching the sky for clues about the world’s existence, its place in the universe, and the order of the heavens above Lazuril. This was new. It was something he had not seen before.
docs.title: The First Gate

docs.text: After passing through the first gate, the party entered Caer Oryn. The capital was already stirring with the pressures of the day: city traffic, working crowds, and the early signs of preparation for Cadris’ Day. Once inside, Nakoa arranged for a letter to be sent back home. The full contents of the letter have not yet been disclosed, but a response is expected in roughly four days.
docs.title: Into Caer Oryn

docs.text: The party then made their way toward the Foundry Quarter. Entry was more difficult than usual because of the preparations for Cadris’ Day. Banners were being hung, work crews were moving through the streets, and the quarter had the ordered disorder of a city preparing itself for public celebration while still trying to keep its industry moving. Two guards blocked the main entry point into the quarter. Teclis attempted to overrule them using his position as Inquisitor-Scriptor, but without proper papers and authority from Voss, the guards refused to let the party through. To create a distraction, Teclis conjured the image and sound of the wife of the guard he was speaking to being intimate with the guard’s best mate and shift-partner, who was standing beside him. The illusion had the intended effect. Horrified by what he appeared to witness, the guard turned on his companion, and the pair began arguing long enough for the group to slip past. The party were not entirely unnoticed, but the guards had more immediate personal concerns to deal with.
docs.title: Entry to the Foundry Quarter

docs.text: The party headed to Magpie Lane and found number 17. Rather than an active office or working address, the building was derelict. A local worker confirmed that it had once served as an office for a shift manager, but no one had worked there in months. Inside, dust had built up in the front room. The place had the stale stillness of a building left unused rather than simply left quiet. In the back room, however, there were signs of a struggle. A chair had been broken, and a table had been overturned. The group searched more closely and noticed a sealed passageway in the back room. Along the vertical line of the hidden door, there was a small hole covered by an illusion of brick mortar. Beyond it was a route down into a hidden basement.
docs.title: 17 Magpie Lane

docs.text: The basement beneath 17 Magpie Lane was filled with barrels. Most appeared to contain old vegetables and simple stores, but tucked behind the barrels was a small gilded chest. At the top of the chest, a small piece of string was exposed. The group approached it cautiously and decided that Nakoa should pull it free. The string was attached to a courier tag similar to the one found in Edrin’s room. Courier: Edrin Vaal Address: 17 Magpie Lane Item: small green lizard figure, Veylrain origin The party did not find or recover the figurine itself. The courier tag only confirmed that such an item had been linked to Edrin Vaal and 17 Magpie Lane. On the advice of the group, Nakoa checked the chest more carefully for traps. He found a small spring-loaded mechanism inside and disabled it before unlocking the chest. The trap had been arranged to smash together a vial of poison and a vial of alchemist’s fire. Beneath the mechanism was more Veylrain cloth. As the group continued their search, they also found blood seeping between the basement floorboards. There were dragged footmarks leading back toward the stairs, suggesting that someone had been wounded or moved through the basement after the struggle above. The blood was human. After securing the dangerous vials and inspecting the surrounding barrels, the party found only old vegetables and simple stored goods. With the chest dealt with and the courier tag recovered, they left 17 Magpie Lane.

docs.text: Session 3: Redstone Revelations ¶ Played: 8 July 2026 Location: Magpie Lane, Caer Oryn to Morfael Starting point: Magpie Lane Back to 17 Magpie Lane ¶ With the rooftop attacker unconscious after the fall from the scaffolds and rooftops, the party moved quickly. They took him back into 17 Magpie Lane and down into the hidden basement beneath the derelict building. They did this unseen. Teclis kept one hand ready with invisibility held close, prepared to hide the captive or the party at a moment’s notice if anyone turned into the lane at the wrong time. The street outside still carried the noise of the Foundry Quarter, but beneath the floorboards of number 17 the air was close, damp, and stained by what had already happened there. The captive was placed on a stool among the barrels. His hands and feet were secured while the party discussed how best to make him talk. Teclis then created an illusion of a guillotine. The image was severe enough to change the mood in the room. It was not merely a threat of violence. It was staged, deliberate, and theatrical. Cassian was visibly uncomfortable with it, the line between justice and cruelty already becoming difficult to ignore. Garron Duskholt ¶ The captive was a human man named Garron Duskholt. As the party forced him down toward the illusion of the guillotine, they noticed a brand burned into the back of his neck: the crying eye mark they had already come to associate with the hidden faction moving behind the events in Morfael and Caer Oryn. When questioned, Garron admitted that the mark belonged to an organisation called the Obsidian Register. At first, he tried to posture. He treated the work as a job, something done for coin and survival rather than conviction. He showed no real remorse for what had happened to Edrin Vaal, for the attack on the party, or for the wider harm caused by the Register’s operations. That lack of remorse struck Cassian hard. Cassian broke Garron’s nose, leaving blood running down his face as the interrogation continued. Nakoa’s claws at Garron’s throat and the fear of the guillotine illusion did the rest. Garron began to give answers. What Garron Revealed ¶ Garron told the party that the drop-off for the lizard idol was at the Gilded Hart, in room 13. He also confirmed that Edrin Vaal had been taken down the drain where the party later fought him, but Garron claimed not to know where Edrin had been taken after that. The drain was a route, not the final destination. When asked about his superior, Garron first tried to give a false name: Johan Schmidt. Alekthar was not convinced. He used detect thoughts, first catching enough from Garron’s surface thoughts to recognise the lie, then pushing deeper. Beneath the false answer, Alekthar found the name Garron was trying not to think about. Odran Kesh. Garron said that Kesh was holed up in the Counting House in the Foundry Quarter of Caer Oryn. When questioned about House Vaelisar, Garron insisted that he did not know what had happened there. He claimed that the Obsidian Register would not risk interfering directly with noble houses. Even so, he also said that body bags had been carried out of the Vaelisar manor, suggesting there had been many deaths inside despite the official silence surrounding the sealing of the house. The End of the Interrogation ¶ With the main line of questioning over, most of the party reached a silent agreement through telepathic communication. Cassian, unable to join that mental exchange through magic, stood apart from that private consensus. Teclis then said his goodbyes. He asked Garron to pick a number between one, two, and three. Garron chose two. Teclis summoned three magical daggers. The first shot past Garron over his shoulder. The third skimmed his ear. The second struck directly into his neck. The force threw Garron backward into the barrels behind him. A moment later, the conjured blades vanished into thin air, leaving the basement quiet except for the aftermath. Inkglass Apothecary ¶ After leaving Magpie Lane, the party travelled to the Academy Quarter during the remaining hours of the morning. Bells rang out across the district, calling students and professors to classes while the city’s scholarly life continued around them. Their destination was Inkglass Apothecary, where they went to visit Quincy Adams. Teclis was greeted warmly. He and Quincy had already built a working relationship, and Quincy received him with open arms rather than suspicion. Teclis asked that Nakoa be treated in the back room, and Quincy’s assistant, Elowen, took charge of his care. Elowen admitted that she had never provided first aid to a tabaxi before, but assured Nakoa that the inner anatomy was surely similar enough, even if there was far more hair on the outside. The Red Dust ¶ The party showed Quincy the red dust collected from Edrin Vaal’s body, including the material found around his teeth and under his nails. Quincy identified it as veinstone. He explained that the name came from the Crimson Chain, where the material was mined. There were different kinds of veinstone, marked by different colours, but red was the most common. Quincy had heard rumours of veinstone being used in weapons and in gemstones designed to channel magic. Some had once been set into staves and wands to enhance spellcasting ability. That sort of use was no longer common. Mining had mostly ceased, and veinstone had become a rare resource, largely held by noble houses and the Crown. Quincy agreed to examine the sample, but warned that he would need more material before he could study it fully. He also explained that the waters around the Godscar have a reddish hue because of veinstone leaching into them. The water is considered fresh, but drinking it in large volumes is not advised. Before the party left, Quincy provided two healing potions at a heavy discount to aid them in their future travels. They said their goodbyes, promising to return in a few days once Quincy had finished inspecting the dust. Return to Morfael ¶ The party then travelled out of Caer Oryn and back down to Morfael. On the way, they discussed the lizard figurine. Nakoa explained that relics like it had been found in the Veylrain Expanse before. He also noted something strange about them: if touched, they could simply vanish, turning to dust. The comment left the object feeling less like ordinary contraband and more like something unstable, old, or deliberately protected against handling. The Chapel of the Last Lantern ¶ Back in Morfael, the party reported to Sister Halva Dorn at the Chapel of the Last Lantern. She told them that Watch-Corporal Dannel Strake had been looking for them. He wanted to know what he should report up the chain, particularly regarding the killing of Edrin Vaal and the party’s involvement in the events at the Flood Steps. Teclis also made clear that he intended to arrange additional funding for the chapel, which was not in a fit state to properly support the work being asked of it. Alekthar then asked whether Old Pell of the Harrowchain Ferry could place items from the chapel’s offering box among any shipments whose manifest bore the Amakiir sigil. The purpose was to create a recognisable marker, allowing the party to identify such shipments later if they came across them. To help remember the objects, Teclis drew several of the offering-box items for future reference. Before leaving the matter with Sister Dorn, the party warned that the townsfolk of Morfael should be more cautious, especially at night. They advised that whatever guards Watch-Corporal Strake could spare should patrol more actively and question or apprehend wandering robed figures. End Point ¶ The session left the party with several clear threads: the Obsidian Register now had a name, Garron Duskholt had pointed them toward the Gilded Hart and room 13, Odran Kesh had been identified at the Counting House in the Foundry Quarter, and Quincy Adams had confirmed the red dust as veinstone. At the same time, House Vaelisar had become more ominous. Garron claimed the Register would not interfere with noble houses, yet body bags had reportedly been carried from the manor. Whatever happened there was larger than a simple civic sealing. The party returned to Morfael with new leads, more questions, and a growing sense that the red stone beneath the city was moving through hands far more organised than a single courier route.

docs.text: Session 4: The Hart of the Matter ¶ Played: 13 July 2026 Location: Morfael to the High Quarter of Caer Oryn Starting point: Chapel of the Last Lantern, Morfael Back to Caer Oryn ¶ The party left Morfael and travelled directly back to Caer Oryn with a clear destination and a plan already forming. The Gilded Hart Hotel. Room 13. It was the location Garron Duskholt had given them during his interrogation, and the same room identified in the courier note connected to the missing lizard figurine. Whatever the Obsidian Register had arranged there, the party intended to find it. After entering the High Quarter, they passed through wide, immaculate streets surrounded by fantastical stores, expensive eateries, private residences and sprawling noble manors. The district was a world apart from the crowded lanes of Morfael and the smoke-stained streets of the Foundry Quarter. Everything appeared carefully maintained, from the pale paving stones beneath their feet to the brass lamps and clipped trees lining the roads. The party stood out, but coin and confidence carried them onward. The Gilded Hart ¶ The Gilded Hart occupied a prominent position on Hartglass Row, its cream-stone frontage illuminated beneath a polished brass-and-glass canopy. Elegantly dressed doormen welcomed the party at the entrance before directing them into the warm, busy reception hall. Marcelline Orras, the hotel’s immaculate proprietor, kept a watchful eye over the establishment while Selda Morn worked behind the reception desk. The party asked about room 13. Unfortunately, it had already been booked. Rather than draw attention by pressing the matter, they arranged rooms of their own nearby. Teclis and Alekthar took the superior room numbered 14, while Nakoa and Cassian booked the standard double room numbered 12. They were now positioned on either side of their target. Dinner with a View ¶ Their stay included a complimentary fine-dining experience, and the party were soon seated together beside one of the dining room’s tall windows. The meal offered a taste of High Quarter excess. Fresh bread, carefully prepared meats, rich sauces, fine accompaniments and plentiful alcohol were brought to the table by attentive staff. For a brief time, the party were able to eat and drink among the city’s wealthy patrons while appearing to be ordinary guests. That pretence did not last long. From their seats beside the window, they noticed a sudden rush of Civic Directorate employees moving along Hartglass Row. The officials were heading in the direction of House Vaelisar. The movement was too hurried and too coordinated to be routine. The Maid Who Survived ¶ The party politely questioned one of the waiters about the Directorate activity and whether he had heard any rumours concerning House Vaelisar. The waiter was reluctant at first, but admitted that he knew a young woman named Resha who had worked as a maid within the Vaelisar household at the time of the incident. Resha had been inside the manor when everything went wrong. Unlike most of the household, she had escaped alive, although she had suffered a severe blow to the head during whatever had occurred within the house. Since losing her position, Resha could often be found at Starflux , a coffee shop situated on the corner of Hartglass Row. The news changed the nature of the party’s investigation. House Vaelisar was no longer merely a sealed ruin filled with second-hand rumours and reports of body bags. There was a living witness. Alekthar Scouts the Manor ¶ During the meal, Alekthar decided to investigate the sudden Directorate movement for himself. Leaving the others at the hotel, he made his way towards House Vaelisar. From a distance, he could see two pike-wielding guards stationed before the front gates. Beyond them stood the manor itself, visibly broken and shattered. Windows had been blown out, sections of the structure had collapsed, and the building showed every sign of having suffered a violent and deeply distressing event. More guards paced within the walls, patrolling the outer grounds surrounding the manor. Alekthar approached the gate and questioned the two men stationed there. What had happened? Why had the Civic Directorate placed the manor under lockdown? Most importantly, who had ordered the property sealed? The guards remained tight-lipped and offered little of substance. Nevertheless, the conversation gave Alekthar enough time to inspect the entrance closely, study the surrounding grounds and gain a better understanding of the number and placement of the men inside. Once he had learned all he could, Alekthar turned to leave. One of the guards called him back. Roderick Valeborne. Valeborne was the man overseeing the sealing of House Vaelisar. Should the party obtain information regarding the incident, or wish to pursue the matter through official channels, he was the man they would need to speak with. Rest and Observation ¶ Following the meal, the party retired to their rooms. They entered separately to avoid drawing unnecessary attention and took the opportunity to rest fully, enjoying comforts rarely available during their travels. The superior room occupied by Teclis and Alekthar was particularly impressive. It was spacious, warmly furnished and opened onto a large balcony overlooking Hartglass Row. From there, they had a clear view across the surrounding streets and towards the damaged Vaelisar manor. It was an excellent vantage point. Due to his elven trance, Teclis completed his rest before the others. He made his way downstairs with the intention of visiting Starflux and locating Resha. Before leaving the hotel, however, he overheard a conversation between a young man dressed in brown leathers and an older gentleman whose bearing immediately suggested a long military career. The older man spoke with the confidence of someone who had survived more than one war. “Them men behind the gate, they ain’t no soldiers. The way they walk, I can tell. The footwork and pacing isn’t right.” Teclis took note. The men guarding House Vaelisar might have been dressed and equipped like soldiers, but according to someone experienced enough to recognise the difference, they were merely pretending. Whatever their true purpose, it was not the ordinary protection of a damaged building. Starflux After Hours ¶ Teclis continued along Hartglass Row until he reached Starflux. Unfortunately, the coffee shop was closed. Teclis, however, had never been particularly accepting of the word “no”. With a click of his fingers, he conjured a large mechanical music box in the middle of the quieting street. The device immediately began blaring out a fine tune, filling Hartglass Row with music that was entirely too loud and far too cheerful for the hour. Teclis waited. It did not take long. A sash window above the coffee shop was thrown open and a woman leaned out. She was not Resha, but the owner and principal barista of Starflux, now roused from her evening by an elf and his magically summoned street orchestra. Teclis apologised for the unusual method of gaining her attention before asking whether she knew Resha. “Of course I know her. Fine young girl. Poor thing lost her job with the trouble at the Vaelisar manor. That’s why I’m advertising for an assistant.” Teclis glanced towards the shopfront and noticed a newly displayed advertisement seeking a barista. The owner explained that the law required her to advertise the position publicly rather than simply giving it to the person she wanted. Nevertheless, the outcome had apparently already been decided. Resha would be arriving the following morning for her first shift. After a brief exchange concerning Resha, the closed shop and the music still echoing along the street, the woman withdrew into the building. As she slammed the sash window shut, Teclis heard her mutter: “Pompous prick.” The Plan for Room 13 ¶ Meanwhile, the rest of the party had begun scheming. Alekthar cast detect magic from room 14, searching for any obvious magical presence beyond the walls that might reveal where the relic had been hidden. Nakoa and Cassian listened closely from room 12, attempting to detect movement within the room between them. They heard nothing. There appeared to be no sign of life within room 13. The coast seemed clear. Cassian positioned himself in the corridor to keep watch. Alekthar moved onto the balcony, from where he could observe the neighbouring room and the street below. Nakoa approached the door to room 13 and began working on the lock. By the time Teclis returned from Starflux and made his way upstairs, Nakoa was already preparing to enter. Teclis joined Cassian in the corridor while Alekthar leaned farther over the balcony, guiding Nakoa from outside as he moved through the room. Inside Room 13 ¶ Nakoa searched the room carefully. At first, nothing appeared unusual. The room looked unoccupied but maintained, as though its resident expected to return without warning. Near the bed, however, Nakoa’s attention was drawn to the rug. Beneath it, one of the floorboards had been disturbed. Fine green dust surrounded its edges, which the party believed might be another variety of veinstone dust. Nakoa prised the board loose. Hidden beneath it were several Veylrain wrappings and a brief handwritten note: Hart / 13 / 3rd bell The relic itself was gone. Unwilling to end the search there, Nakoa moved to the dresser. Among the papers inside, he discovered a small personal information form. It read: Name: Derren Kerr Birth Location: Karthrest Occupation: Travelling metals broker The writing on the form did not look natural. The name appeared to have been written over something else or altered after the form was originally completed. Derren Kerr was almost certainly a false identity. The Wrong Man ¶ While Nakoa continued searching, Teclis and Cassian heard footsteps approaching along the corridor. Someone was heading directly towards them. This could be the occupant of room 13. Thinking quickly, Teclis conjured the sound of a tremendous roar behind the approaching man. The illusion had the desired effect. Terrified, the man rushed forwards towards Teclis and Cassian, fumbling desperately with a set of keys. The pair prepared to intercept him. Instead, the frightened guest scrambled past them, unlocked room 10 and disappeared inside. They had terrified an innocent hotel guest. It was not their man. Derren Kerr ¶ With their search complete, Nakoa withdrew from room 13 and the party regrouped. They gathered the Veylrain wrappings, the note, the suspicious green dust and the forged personal details before heading downstairs. They questioned Selda Morn about the room’s occupant. Selda confirmed that room 13 was registered to Derren Kerr . Kerr was not a recent guest. He had maintained the booking for some time and paid to keep room 13 available almost permanently, even during periods when he was apparently absent from the hotel. The room was more than temporary accommodation. It was a fixed meeting point, hiding place or drop location maintained under a false name. The note beneath the floorboards suggested that another exchange was connected to the Gilded Hart at third bell, but whether it referred to an earlier meeting or one yet to take place remained unclear. The Third Bell Debate ¶ As the party prepared to leave for House Vaelisar under the cover of dark, Cassian stopped them. What if the third bell did not refer to the day, but to the early hours of the morning? What if Derren Kerr intended to return to room 13 at night? If they left now, they might miss him entirely. The group deliberated for a few tense moments. It was a reasonable fear and a dangerous possibility. In the end, however, they came to the conclusion that they had to risk it. Whatever waited inside House Vaelisar felt too urgent, too threatening and too important to ignore until morning. They would move on the manor now. Over the Wall ¶ The party used what they had learned earlier about the manor’s exterior and its patrol patterns. Knowing that the interior patrols had thinned, they chose not to approach the front entrance and instead skirted the perimeter, moving through darkness towards the outer wall. Nakoa went first. With feline grace, he scaled the wall quickly and almost effortlessly. Just as he reached the top, he caught a paw on the stone and tumbled over the far side. Fortunately, instinct and agility took over. He flipped forward in one smooth motion and landed in a way that almost made the blunder look deliberate. A shame none of the others saw it properly. It had, in truth, looked rather swish. Alekthar and Teclis followed with the aid of a rope. Then came Cassian. Cassian was not built for skulking. Heavy armour and stealth work had never been natural companions, and despite hauling himself over the wall with solid effort and strength, it was the descent that undid him. He came down hard on the other side with a heavy thud, landing on his feet but striking the ground with enough force that it seemed to shake beneath them. The others froze. Their eyes shot towards the front approach where the guards stirred at the sound. One of them turned his head and half-heartedly scanned the darkness, but the effort was lazy and uncertain. Whether through arrogance, carelessness or poor training, the outer watch failed to follow up properly. The party had slipped in. The Rear Approach ¶ Quickly retrieving the rope, the group hurried after Alekthar through the gardens towards the rear of the manor, aiming for the gardening hut that connected to the larger house. As they approached, they noticed something new. A throbbing hum vibrated through the night air. It was not loud, but it was impossible to ignore once heard. It was the sound of energy under pressure, a subtle and persistent thrum that seemed to press against the skin as much as the ear. They found the rear doors unlocked. Once inside, the strange hum became stronger. It did not come from directly ahead so much as from above and somewhere deeper within the structure, as though the house itself had become a resonating chamber for something unnatural. They paused and looked upward, but could see nothing. Then they pressed on. Following the sound, they moved through the servant-side pathways and deeper into the manor’s interior. The Central Hall ¶ At last, they opened a door into the manor’s central hall. The room beyond had been wrecked. The central space was shattered and dilapidated, a noble chamber broken open into ruin. Wooden walls were splintered. Fine floor tiles had been cracked apart or torn loose entirely, the ground littered with fragments of ceramic and broken debris. Furniture had been tossed aside and smashed against the outer walls. Blood had been smeared across torn tapestries and painted surfaces, leaving dark streaks that seemed almost black in the moonlit gloom. The hum was louder here than anywhere else. The air was stale and unnaturally cold, especially for a summer’s night. They looked upward. The ceiling had been torn open, revealing a great hole into the upper floor where shattered boards hung jagged and broken. Beyond that, parts of the roof had given way as well, letting moonlight spill down into the wreckage. And there, suspended in the ruined vertical space between the floors, hung the source of it all. A black orb. It floated motionless in the air, heavy and wrong, as if it had more weight than the room could bear and yet no need of support. Its surface was not smooth but fractured, the darkness split by dim veins of red that pulsed deep within like banked embers trapped beneath stone. Every so often a faint red crackle spilled across its shell, thin and momentary, gone almost as soon as it appeared. The sound filling the hall came from it. A low and ceaseless vibration. A presence rather than a noise. The orb did not blaze. It did not lash out. It simply hung there in dreadful stillness, humming softly in the cold dark, as though it were waiting for the house, the night, or the people staring at it to realise what had already happened. And with that sight before them, the session came to an end.

docs.text: The party left Morfael and travelled directly back to Caer Oryn with a clear destination and a plan already forming. The Gilded Hart Hotel. Room 13. It was the location Garron Duskholt had given them during his interrogation, and the same room identified in the courier note connected to the missing lizard figurine. Whatever the Obsidian Register had arranged there, the party intended to find it. After entering the High Quarter, they passed through wide, immaculate streets surrounded by fantastical stores, expensive eateries, private residences and sprawling noble manors. The district was a world apart from the crowded lanes of Morfael and the smoke-stained streets of the Foundry Quarter. Everything appeared carefully maintained, from the pale paving stones beneath their feet to the brass lamps and clipped trees lining the roads. The party stood out, but coin and confidence carried them onward.
docs.title: Back to Caer Oryn

docs.text: The Gilded Hart occupied a prominent position on Hartglass Row, its cream-stone frontage illuminated beneath a polished brass-and-glass canopy. Elegantly dressed doormen welcomed the party at the entrance before directing them into the warm, busy reception hall. Marcelline Orras, the hotel’s immaculate proprietor, kept a watchful eye over the establishment while Selda Morn worked behind the reception desk. The party asked about room 13. Unfortunately, it had already been booked. Rather than draw attention by pressing the matter, they arranged rooms of their own nearby. Teclis and Alekthar took the superior room numbered 14, while Nakoa and Cassian booked the standard double room numbered 12. They were now positioned on either side of their target.
docs.title: The Gilded Hart

docs.text: Their stay included a complimentary fine-dining experience, and the party were soon seated together beside one of the dining room’s tall windows. The meal offered a taste of High Quarter excess. Fresh bread, carefully prepared meats, rich sauces, fine accompaniments and plentiful alcohol were brought to the table by attentive staff. For a brief time, the party were able to eat and drink among the city’s wealthy patrons while appearing to be ordinary guests. That pretence did not last long. From their seats beside the window, they noticed a sudden rush of Civic Directorate employees moving along Hartglass Row. The officials were heading in the direction of House Vaelisar. The movement was too hurried and too coordinated to be routine.

House Vaelisar was no longer merely a sealed ruin filled with second-hand rumours and reports of body bags. There was a living witness.

docs.text: Lazuril is the known world upon which the continent of Arkhaven exists. The world is dominated by vast oceans, separated continental landmasses, deep climatic variation, ancient religious history, and long-lived civilisations whose records often contradict one another. The name "Lazuril" is commonly associated with the blue appearance of the world when viewed through astronomical instruments or described in older cosmological writings. Overview ¶ Lazuril contains multiple continents, major ocean systems, isolated island chains, polar regions, and large unexplored territories. Only portions of the world are well documented. Most surviving historical records originate from: Arkhaven Elven archive houses Dwarven engineering records Religious institutions Maritime trade powers Large sections of the world remain poorly mapped. Astronomy ¶ The study of astronomy is practiced by scholars, navigators, Scriptors, sailors, and religious observatories throughout Lazuril. Several major cultures maintain differing cosmological models regarding: The movement of celestial bodies The divine structure of the heavens The origins of the world The role of magic in the cosmos The relationship between the gods and the stars Astronomical observation is especially important for navigation and calendar keeping. Continents ¶ Arkhaven is currently the best documented continent in surviving records. Other continental landmasses are known to exist beyond the surrounding seas, though many remain politically or geographically distant from the affairs of Arkhaven. Some are known primarily through: Merchant records Sailor testimony Pilgrimage accounts Diplomatic reports Fragmentary maps Ancient archive references Oceans and Seas ¶ The oceans of Lazuril are major drivers of trade, migration, climate, and political influence. Long-distance travel remains dangerous due to: Storm systems Sea monsters Navigational uncertainty Piracy Uncharted waters Seasonal currents Despite this, maritime trade connects large parts of the known world. Historical Ages ¶ Most historians divide the history of Lazuril into broad historical ages. Exact dates remain disputed. Major eras commonly referenced include: The Age Before Memory The Age of Fracture The Post-Godscar Era The Era of Silence The Age of False Saints The Compact Era These classifications are used differently between cultures and institutions. Religion ¶ Religion is one of the defining forces of Lazuril. The gods are widely accepted as real entities capable of interacting with the mortal world through divine magic, prophecy, visions, omens, and miracles. At the same time, the history of Lazuril demonstrates that divine claims can be manipulated, misunderstood, or falsified. This tension heavily influences politics, scholarship, and law. Current Status ¶ Lazuril remains politically fragmented and historically incomplete. Ancient ruins, disputed records, forgotten roads, submerged structures, and lost civilisations continue to shape the modern world. Many scholars believe significant portions of Lazurilian history remain undiscovered, concealed, or deliberately restricted.
